H.S. Madaan, J.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that plaintiff Labh Kaur had brought a suit for recovery of Rs.70,000/- against Sucha Singh defendant on the averments that the latter had borrowed a sum of Rs.70,000/- from her on 19.02.1983 executing a pronote and receipt in her favour undertaking to return the loan amount with interest @ 1% per month.
That pronote and receipt were thumb marked by the defendant in the presence of witnesses.
Subsequently, the plaintiff asked the defendant to return the principle amount with interest but he refused to do so giving rise to a cause of action to the plaintiff to bring the suit in question.

2. On getting notice, the defendant appeared and offered a contest by filing a written statement,
raising various legal objections 1 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:030947 RSA-419-1991 (O&M) -2- and on merits, denying that he had borrowed any amount from the plaintiff or executed any pronote and receipt in her favour.

He added that the plaintiff had filed a complaint under Sucha Singh vs Labh Kaur on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184831173/
1 Section 420 IPC against the defendant, in connection with that, the defendant was summoned to the police station where SI Mann Singh had obtained his thumb impression on some papers which might have been converted into pronote and receipt.

3. The plaintiff filed replication, controverting the allegations in the written statement whereas reiterating the averments in the plaint.

4. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed:-
1.

Whether the defendant Sucha Singh has borrowed Rs.70,000/-
from the plaintiff on 19.2.1983 and executed pronote and receipt in lieu of that?

OPP. 
2. If issue No.1 proved whether the pronote and receipt are without consideration?

OPD. 
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to recover Rs.95000/-?

OPP. 
4. Whether the plaintiff has no locus standi and cause of action to file this suit?
OPD 5.
Whether the suit is not maintainable in the present form?

OPD. 
6. Whether the plaintiff is estopped from filing this suit by her act and conduct?

OPD. 
7. Whether the plaint has not been properly verified?
If so its effect?

OPD. 
8. Whether the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to try this suit?

OPD. 
9. Whether the suit is not properly valued for the purpose of court 2 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:030947 RSA-419-1991 (O&M) -3- fee and jurisdiction?

OPD. 
10.Relief.
5. Parties were afforded adequate opportunities to lead evidence in support of their respective claims.
During the course of evidence of plaintiff, she got her statement recorded as PW1 and repeated on oath her case as given in the plaint.
She further examined PW2 Gian Singh, an attesting witness of pronote and receipt and PW-3 Virender Bhushan, document expert.
6. In rebuttal, the defendant got his statement recorded as DW1 and repeated on oath his case as given in the written statement.
He further examined DW2 Shisha Singh, an attesting witness of pronote and receipt.

sentences.text:
After hearing arguments, the trial Court of Sub Judge, Ist Class, Sunam decided issue No.1 in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant, holding that defendant Sucha Singh had borrowed a sum of Rs.70,000/- from the plaintiff on 19.02.1983 and had executed pronote Ex.P1 and receipt Ex.P2 in her favour whereas issue No.2 was decided against the defendant holding that pronote and receipt were for consideration; issue No.3 was decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant holding that plaintiff is entitled to recover amount of Rs.70,000/- with interest @1% per month, total Rs.95,000/- from the defendant; issue No.4 was decided against the defendant holding that Rs.95,000/- are due from defendant to the plaintiff ,and he 3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:030947 RSA-419-1991 (O&M) -4- is liable to pay the same to her and non-payment of amount gave locus standi and a cause of action to the plaintiff to bring the suit;
issue No.5 was decided against the defendant, holding that the suit was maintainable; issues No.6 and 7 were decided against the defendant; issue No.8 was decided against the defendant holding that civil Court at Sunam had jurisdiction to entertain and try the suit; issue No.9 was decided against the defendant holding that required Court fee had been paid.

As a result of findings on the issues, the suit of the plaintiff was decreed for recovery of Rs.95,000/- with costs with future interest @ 6% per annum from the date of institution of suit till date of realization, vide judgment and decree dated 01.08.1987.

8. Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, the defendant had preferred an appeal before District Judge, Sangrur, that appeal was however, dismissed by District Judge, Sangrur, vide judgment dated 24.01.1990.

9. Still feeling aggrieved, the defendant had approached this Court by way of filing the present Regular Second Appeal, notice of which was issued to the respondent/plaintiff who had initially put in appearance through counsel but subsequently, stopped putting in appearance.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant besides going through the record and I find that there is absolutely no merit in the appeal.

Here both the Courts in view of the pleadings of the parties by proper appraisal and appreciation of evidence and correct 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:030947 RSA-419-1991 (O&M) -5- interpretation of law have returned concurrent findings that defendant Sucha Singh had borrowed a sum of Rs.70,000/- from the plaintiff on 19.02.1983 executing pronote Ex.P1 and receipt Ex.P2 in her favour, undertaking to return the loan amount with interest @ 1% per month but he failed to do so despite demand in that regard having been raised by the plaintiff from the defendant.

The version set up by the defendant that as a matter of fact, he had not borrowed any amount from the plaintiff and on a complaint under Section 420 IPC having been submitted by the plaintiff against him at police station, he was summoned there where SI Mann Singh had obtained his thumb impression on blank papers, which might have been converted into pronote and receipt, however, he had not received any consideration amount was considered and rejected, mainly for the reason that till date no complaint had been made by the defendant before any authority in that regard and further presumption under Section 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act was there that the pronote and negotiable instrument had been drawn for consideration.
Sucha Singh vs Labh Kaur on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184831173/
3 11. Furthermore from the statement of PW-3 Varinder Bhushan, Finger Print Expert, it stood established that thumb impressions on pronote and receipt were those of the defendant. To prove her case, plaintiff had got her statement recorded as PW1 and corroboration to her version came from the side of PW2 Gian Singh, an attesting witness of pronote and receipt.

Although, defendant appearing as DW1 had deposed inconsonance with his case pleaded in the written 5 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:030947 RSA-419-1991 (O&M) -6- statement but his testimony does not inspire confidence.
DW2 Shisha Singh other attesting witness of pronote and receipt had though stated that their thumb impressions had been obtained on blank papers, however.
Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 were not writing on the blank paper.
He had stated that pronote was written in the police station and in his presence thumb impressions of Sucha Singh were not obtained.
Shisha Singh is common relative of plaintiff Labh Kaur and defendant Sucha Singh, therefore, the stand taken by him does not help the defendant much in advancing his case.

This being the state of affairs, I do not see any reason to interfere with the judgments passed by the Courts below which do not suffer from any illegality or infirmity, rather the Regular Second Appeal is found to be without merit and no substantial question of law arises in this appeal.
The appeal is found to be without merit and is dismissed accordingly.
